release.name: Wallify 0.7.15
release.notes:
- From 0.7.15, fixed: **live wallpapers taking turns changed in front of you when the screen came on** - the
  real cause. Painting the next video's first frame when the screen went off could crash Wallify Live inside the
  graphics driver (a poster of odd width, read past its end); Android restarted it, and the new wallpaper then
  loaded while you were looking. Posters are drawn safely now: the change happens with the screen off.
- From 0.7.14: **favourites wallpaper no longer changes in front of you when the screen comes on** - the next
  wallpaper's picture is now decoded ahead, while the current one is showing, so the moment the screen goes off it
  is only drawn (it used to be decoded right then, and on a phone that fell asleep first it appeared after the
  screen lit up). A change that arrives as the screen goes off is never played or faded any more either.
- From 0.7.13, fixed: **a live wallpaper moved off-centre stood still** - after dragging or zooming a video in
  *Set*, the wallpaper showed its first frame as a still picture (or black). The framing now gets the screen size
  and the video plays; if a phone's GPU still shows nothing within 4 s, it plays centred instead of standing still.
- From 0.7.12, fixed: **the same wallpaper twice in a row of categories** - many wallpapers are in more than one
  category (Universe and Dark, say). When the feed moved on by itself to the next category, the ones you had just
  seen came back at its end. They no longer do; a category you pick yourself still shows all of it.
- From 0.7.11, fixed (developer counts): *All* shows how many wallpapers the library really holds (1,597 live), not
  the categories added up - a wallpaper in two categories was counted twice (2,578).
- From 0.7.10: **one tap answers at once** - full screen in and out with no wait (a short, small badge at your
  finger and the buttons sliding away, no vibration). Two taps love it with the heart in the **middle of the
  screen**; the first of the two taps is simply taken back, so the buttons stay.
- From 0.7.9: **double-tap to love it** - two taps on a wallpaper love it with a heart in Wallify's colours that pops
  where your finger was, with a ring and sparks (keep tapping for more hearts). **One tap** is full screen and back:
  a small badge pops at your finger and the buttons slide away - and come back with a little bounce. These effects
  play even on phones where Android's animations are switched off (they used to vanish in the same moment there).
- From 0.7.8: **Set favorites wallpaper** shows a fanned deck of your favourites and the "how often" scale again (a
  bar of stops, like the speed bar) instead of a list - each time the screen turns on is still the default.
- From 0.7.8: the **Set screen**: pull the panel down (or tap the wallpaper) to see the wallpaper alone - the back
  arrow is shown then, and a small handle at the bottom brings the panel back. *Send to TV* shows only while one of
  your TVs is on and reachable.
- From 0.7.8: **Settings** - *Autoplay on mobile data* is gone (videos always play); *Keep live wallpaper on* shows
  only until you allow it; *My screens* is now *TV screens*.
- From 0.7.7, fixed: **a category shows all of its wallpapers.** A category you had already seen much of ended
  after the few new ones - "88" on its tab, four wallpapers in it - because the ones you had seen were left out and
  never came back. Now the new ones still come first, and every wallpaper you have seen follows them (the ones
  seen longest ago first), so a category is always as long as its number says.
- From 0.7.6: **the next wallpaper is already there when you turn the screen on.** The favorites wallpaper used to
  change when the screen came on - on some phones a moment later, in front of your eyes. It now changes when the
  screen goes *off*: the next photo or live wallpaper is put in place right then, and a live one starts from that
  very picture when you look at the phone again.
- From 0.7.6: **a soft fade** when the wallpaper changes while you are looking at it (on a timer, *Next wallpaper
  now*, lock screen to home screen) - from live to live, live to photo and back - instead of a hard cut.
- From 0.7.6: **how often** - *Set favorites wallpaper* now asks how often it should change: each time the screen
  turns on (the default), or every minute, 5, 15 or 30 minutes, hour, 3 hours or day. The bar in Love it's gallery
  view opens the same choice while it runs (*Save*, *Stop*).
- From 0.7.5: **Set favorites wallpaper** - one button under *Set wallpaper* (and a bar in Love it's gallery
  view): every wallpaper you love, photos and live alike, takes turns on your screen. The *Auto-change* screen
  (photos or live, which ones) is gone. A wallpaper
  you love later joins by itself, one you take out leaves; tap the button again to stop. *Send to TV* shows only
  with a TV connected (connecting one: Settings → My screens). The play and round-arrows buttons at the top of Love
  it are gone, and the tabs there no longer run under the button next to them.
- From 0.7.5: **always something to see** - opening Wallify shows a wallpaper at once (the first ones are kept on
  the phone from your last visit), and swiping quickly no longer lands on empty pages: what lies ahead is loaded
  while you swipe, not only when you stop, and each wallpaper's preview is much lighter to show. A page that is
  still on its way shows the wallpaper's own colour with a light moving over it instead of black.
- From 0.7.5, fixed: on some phones *Set live wallpaper* did not bring up Android's screen where you choose home
  screen, lock screen or both (it showed the phone's list of live wallpapers, an older copy of that screen, or
  nothing). It now always opens that screen, and Wallify notices that the wallpaper was set when you come back.
- **Everything is open to everyone**: no Premium, no paywall, no ads. The gallery (Discover) with search and
  filters, and your own videos as live wallpap

release.notes:
TrustAPK 1.8.1070 (build 2070)

Live traffic: reuse built rows when scrolling back (#21)

Every getView built a whole row (a dozen views) even when scrolling back
to a row the list had just shown. The adapter now keeps the rows built
for the current data and gives one back when the list hands it in as the
recycled view for the same position; any notifyDataSetChanged clears them,
so a changed row is always rebuilt. A reused swipe row is snapped shut.

WatchIPTV 1.0.1 for phone, Android TV and Wear OS.

| file | what |

release.name: Touchless Bridge 1.1.22
release.notes:
**Installing over 1.1.21 or older: remove the old app first, once.** This version is signed with a new key, so
Android won't install it on top of an older copy ("App not installed"). Uninstall Touchless Bridge, install
1.1.22, then connect the phone and sign in to HackerAI again. Later versions update in place as before.

A new look, an easier start, a new icon, and the app now shows when HackerAI is working.

- **You can see HackerAI working.** While HackerAI works in the chat, the app's icon in the status bar moves, and
  the notification says "HackerAI is working" with the step it is on right now ("Thinking...", "Opening Maps",
  "Phone tool: get battery status", "Running a command: nmap") and a running clock. Opened, it lists the last few
  steps. Home shows the same line. It keeps following after you close the chat window, and goes quiet when
  HackerAI is done. Only a short line per step is shown, never a command's arguments or its output.
- **The chat stays where you left it.** Closing the chat window no longer throws the page away: open it again and
  it is there at once, also in the middle of a task. A chat left idle for 10 minutes is let go and loads fresh.
- **`touchless … --say "…"` and `--done` work on the phone too** (when the phone itself is the HackerAI machine),
  as they do on a computer. The setup prompt now shows the real form: `touchless call <tool> key=value`.
- **New icon.** A hooded figure whose face is a terminal prompt (`>_`). It also has a themed-icon version, and the
  "Running" notification uses it.
- **Home shows where you stand.** A status card with the phone, Touchless and HackerAI as three points on a line.
  When the phone is connected a glowing packet travels from it to Touchless, and on to HackerAI once you're signed
  in there; while the phone isn't connected nothing moves. A button takes you to HackerAI.
- **The animation shows on every phone**, also where the phone's own animations are turned off. Settings › about ›
  "Animate the status" turns it off.
- **One thing to do on Home: connect your phone.** With a Paste button, and "Open Touchless", which opens the
  Touchless app to copy your address. Once the phone is connected the card folds away and HackerAI opens by itself.
- **HackerAI in the middle of the bottom bar.** One tap from anywhere.
- **Settings in cards.** Connection, HackerAI, always on, about. A line that isn't connected takes you back to
  Home. Running the bridge on the phone itself is now one switch in the connection list, "Remote Control on this
  phone". The setup prompt can be sent again, not only copied.
- **"Check for updates" answers.** It says "No newer version found" when there is nothing newer.
- **Battery.** Settings shows when battery use is already unrestricted, and the button only when it isn't.
- **The chat shows a page loading** with a thin line along the top.
- **Back from Settings** returns to Home.

release.name: v2.1.2
release.notes:
## אבג ABC 2.1.2

- כשחוזרים אחורה למסך (למשל מאות אחת אל רשימת האותיות), ההוראה שלו לא נשמעת שוב. כל מסך מסביר את עצמו רק בפעם הראשונה שנכנסים אליו.
- אחרי לחיצה על אריח, שם הפעילות נשמע עד הסוף לפני ההוראה של המסך החדש, ולא נקטע באמצע.

release.name: Israel App Manager 1.0.3
release.notes:
- **Always the newest version.** The app no longer waits for its catalog to notice a release: every time the list is loaded it asks each app's releases page on GitHub itself, and offers a release the moment it is out.
- **Install and Update check once more** at the moment you tap them, so what gets installed is the newest release, never one that needs another update right after.
- Coming back to the app after a few minutes refreshes the list on its own; pulling down always does.
- Update notifications and the app's own update use the same check.
